label: Mid/late input positions (t=4-7) and the <DEL> step, before copying starts
explanation: Position feature tied to absolute step t during encoding. It never fires at t=0-2 or anywhere in the copy phase, and is rare at t=3 and t>=8. Firing rate peaks at t=5-6 (about 45%, 4-5x lift) for both original tokens and the <DEL> step; <DEL> steps hold 32% of the mass. Within the window it fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1 holds 89% of the mass), and is a bit more likely after certain previous tokens (c 2.9x, then n, w, v, z). The largest activations are at <DEL> or t=5-6 right after a c. The predicate (phase<=1, 4<=t<=7) covers 97% of activations and 98% of the mass, but only about 43% of the steps it selects are active. Which steps inside the window fire depends on token content in a way no simple token-set predicate captured (restricting to first occurrences or to seen tokens lowered F1).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: c, n, w, v, z, e; least: r, g, m, p) and the input two steps back (most: c, 2, n, f, z, j; least: <DEL>, r, m, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
